c101.text: This is Basil. Basil is sitting in an ice box.

c102.text: Yep, that's me. You're probably wondering how I got here.

c103.text: Basil! Your race with Uncle Lim starts in three minutes!

c104.text: And your bike has no bell, no chain and no brakes!

c106.text: Basil is not an expert at bicycles.

f201.text: Three minutes! Which fix gets Basil racing?

f202.text: Fix one: no fixing. I just pedal faster!

f203.text: Fix two: put all three parts back. I made a checklist.

f204.text: Fix three: put the chain and the brakes back, and skip the bell. A bell can't make you go!

f207.text: Show me one, two or three fingers!

p209.text: Let's test them! But first: ten minutes earlier...

s301.text: Uncle Lim's old bike is full of useless parts. Mine won't be. LIGHTER IS FASTER!

b401.text: Who needs a bell? I'm faster as well!

b402.text: Um... but what does THAT part do?

b404.text: But WHY does it go ring?

b407.text: A bell warns people, and pigeons, that you are coming. Basil is not an expert at bells.

b408.text: I have made some new friends.

n501.text: Who needs a chain? It's a greasy pain!

n503.text: It goes round and round. That's all.

n504.text: But WHY does it go round and round?

n505.text: To make my tail greasy. Off it comes!

n506.text: Without a chain, the pedals cannot turn the back wheel.

n507.text: The slowest overtake in history. Let's see it again, in slow motion.

n508.text: Basil, you just lost to a snail.

k601.text: To the ramp! Who needs brakes? Speed is all it takes!

k604.text: Brakes slow you down. Winners never slow down!

k605.text: But WHY would anybody want to slow down?

k610.text: Then nothing can slow its wheels down. It can't stop!

k611.text: We need something big to stop it! The ice box!

k612.text: Brakes help a bike slow down and stop safely. Basil is fine. Basil is a little cold.

k613.text: Don't do this at home. Seriously.

r701.text: In a world... where one lizard thought a bell was too heavy... one race decides everything.

r703.text: Slowly, slowly lah. Where got need to rush?

r707.text: Basil's pedals turn, but nothing joins them to the back wheel. Pedalling faster cannot do the chain's job.

r708.text: But WHY did the old, heavy bike win?

l801.text: Look closer at Uncle Lim's bike.

l802.text: His bell warns people that he is coming. His brakes slow him down at the corner.

l803.text: And his chain turns the back wheel when he pedals!

l804.text: Every part has its own special job, called its function.

l805.text: So my useless parts all had functions.

l806.text: I told you s... Nice try, Basil.

l807.text: His bike is heavier, but it won, because all its parts work together.

j901.text: Be one little link of Uncle Lim's chain! Shrink down. Quietly.

j902.text: The front gear's teeth fit into your gaps, and pull you forward. The whole chain moves, and tugs the back gear round.

j904.text: Pedals, front gear, chain, back gear, wheel. Each part acts on the next one. Scientists say the parts interact.

j905.text: Okay. I want my parts back.

v1001.text: Every part has a job. Brakes, stop me. No more mistakes!

v1002.text: Every part has a job. Chain, turn my wheel again!

v1003.text: Chain and brakes! That's my fix three! Race time!

v1006.text: Quick question! Without a bell, can the bike still move? Think about it.

v1007.text: It can still move, but it is not as safe!

v1008.text: Yes! When one part stops working, the whole bike is likely to be affected.

v1009.text: Every part has a job. Bell, you warn them well!

v1010.text: So a system is made up of different parts...

v1012.text: ...and the parts interact. My bike is a system!

e1102.text: Look closer. Your bones and muscles move your legs. Your heart beats faster, and you breathe faster. Your body is made up of systems too.

e1103.text: And the rain tree is a system. Its roots, stem and leaves each have a function.

w1201.text: Now, here are the words that earn marks.

w1203.text: A system is made up of different parts. Each part has its own function. The parts interact to perform a function. When one part stops working, the whole system is likely to be affected.

e1301.text: But wait. Somebody is still racing!

e1303.text: Aiyoh, boy. Slowly, slowly also can win one, mah. Every part working together!

e1304.text: Picked fix two? You win a point, and so does Pip!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
